title: Looking to create three puzzles based on a library / the Dewey Decimal system

posts.author: TheFrenzy
posts.body:
Greetings everyone,
I am not a game designer on the level of most of you. I made a few games back in college (circa 2005) with RPG Maker XP, but these days I'm just a dad who is trying to help his young son get into game design. Starting this year, my son wanted to design a fan game for one of his favorite "horror mascot" franchises (yes, he is 100% Gen Alpha) and so I got RPG Maker MV.
I don't have a ton a time, but I've re-familiarized myself with most of the mechanics, made some custom sprites and enemies, and so far we've knocked out 2.5 of the envisioned 7 chapters. Our most recent chapter featured a series a music puzzles—figuring out a code on a series of pianos, tuning instruments, and a rhythm challenge.
Now in chapter three we need to put the player through 2-4 library-based puzzles. My initial thought is using something like the Dewey Decimal system to reveal codes, but I'm hitting a bit of puzzle-maker's block trying to think through how to set it up without 1) expecting a player to already know the system or 2) leaving them to simply grab books randomly until they get the needed code. The main challenge seems to be that I'm trying to use the call number system backwards (I definitely think it's possible) because I'm wanting to give them a title and then have them find the call number.
If anyone wants to spitball a few library/book-based ideas for a small series of puzzles, you'd really be helping out this dad.

posts.body:
Thank you for the reply!
ShadowDragon said:
what do you mean number system backwards?
Click to expand...
What I was referring to is that in a real library, you get the Dewey Decimal call number and then go find the book on the shelf. I'm trying to think of a creative way to give the player either the title or hints about the title and then they go find the book on the shelf—in the process, finding the call number for the book and plugging that in for the code.
ShadowDragon said:
what kind of puzzle exactly
Click to expand...
The previous chapter was music themed and I was able to put together those events pretty well because I had a clear idea of how they would work.
I have a pretty good idea of the puzzles for the chapter after this one—with one level being filled with pipes and platforms, the next being a series of turn-on-the-lights-to-find-your-way-through-the-dark puzzles, and the last being filled with non-Euclidean mazes.
It's really just this one library chapter that I'm kind of beating my head against the wall to think of fitting puzzles and mechanics. Possible ideas are:
- Gather clues about a book's title, then find the book, get the call number, enter the call number as the missing code
- Something involving moving bookshelves (a play on the old film trope of secret passage ways hidden behind bookshelves)
- Scraps of paper containing clues hidden inside various books
- A book written in an unknown language and the player has to collect pieces of the cipher to reveal the coded message

posts.author: utunnels
posts.body:
Secret code puzzles are game design cliches but they usually work well to fill the game play.
Maybe the player can find a clue note left by some one, that hints various categories of books. On  each shelf there is a number corresponding to the category. The shelf can be push (or there are hidden buttons behind books) in an order that open a hidden passage or something.
The clues on the note don't have to contain numbers nor directly state the name of the category. It depends on your writing skill but the idea is there. For example, mysteries that go beyond this world referring to 520 astronomy. The puzzle can have extra layers if you blend the words in a poem, a seemingly unrelated article or have multiple clues. There could be hints for example a librarian mentioning the categories and numbers(can be found on the shelves) by complaining some misplaced books.
